title: Pressed Ricotta Ravioli with Lemon and an Olive Oil Emulsion
changes_from_base: The ricotta is pressed between towels to dry it, seasoned with lemon juice, nutmeg and more parmesan, and the ravioli are tossed in an olive oil and pasta-water emulsion instead of butter.
summary: Pillowy ravioli filled with lemon-brightened ricotta and parmesan, coated in a silky sauce drawn together from oil and starchy pasta water.
equipment: fluted pasta wheel or sharp knife

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fresh egg pasta sheets (shop-bought, or homemade fresh egg pasta)
fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water
extra-virgin olive oil, plus more at the table

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Lay 565 g ricotta across a tea towel on a rimmed tray, top with a second towel and press hard, wait 5 min, then scrape it into a bowl.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Mix in 115 g parmesan, ¼ tsp nutmeg, 2 tsp lemon juice, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: For homemade, split 450 g dough into 4 and roll each piece in turn to just under 2 mm, trimming every sheet to roughly 38 x 13 cm.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: For hand-shaped ravioli, crease a sheet lengthways, space 6 heaped tablespoons of filling 1 cm apart, dampen the top with water, fold it over and press the air out, then slice into 6 squares with a fluted wheel.

steps.title: Mould
steps.text: Or lay a sheet over a ravioli mould, press hollows into it, drop in about 1 tbsp each, cover with a second sheet and run a pin across until the ridges appear.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Lower into plenty of boiling water with 1 tbsp salt and cook for about 3 min until they float, saving 120 ml of the water.

steps.title: Emulsify
steps.text: Tip the ravioli and saved water back into the pot with 60 ml oil and stir gently over high heat for about 1 min to a creamy sauce.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate up straight away with extra olive oil to pass round.

tips: Pressing the ricotta first firms the filling so the parcels seal neatly.
Freeze shaped parcels on a lined tray, then bag them for up to 2 months and cook from frozen with an extra 30 seconds.
Keep the heat high and stir quickly so the oil and water bind into a glossy sauce.
storage: Chill leftovers and eat within 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
